The TTAP spokesperson cautioned that the national government must not become an alternative to the people’s mandate or a permanent political arrangement. Its sole purpose should be to facilitate elections and transfer power to representatives chosen by the electorate, he emphasised.

“Pakistan needs neither an imposed political arrangement nor a government established through political expediency,” he said, adding that the authority to govern must flow exclusively from the free and fair vote of the people.

He said the ultimate objective should be a country governed under one Constitution, an independent electoral system and a government that genuinely represented the will of the people.

articles.title: Bilawal terms PTI a ‘political reality’, calls for restoring its trust in the ‘system’
articles.summary:
PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Thursday asserted that PTI was a “political reality” whose trust in the “system” needs to be restored for a political reset to take place.

Bilawal made the remarks while speaking at another “Meet the Press” event, this time at the Multan Press Club. The Bhutto scion is on a visit to Punjab for the past few days, making stops in Multan, Dera Ghazi Khan and Muzaffargarh so far.

Responding to a query about him calling former premier Imran Khan a “political prisoner”, Bilawal explained that he made the “controversial” statement in a polarised political environment, where those terming him a political prisoner could not be convinced otherwise and those declaring him a convict and corrupt could not be convinced otherwise.

Bilawal stressed that in his speech, not the press queries, he made an observation that was not about Imran, but rather about Pakistan’s political history wherein elected premiers often end up going to jail later on or come to power after being imprisoned.

“Whatever opinion you may hold about Khan sahib, even if you think he is not a political prisoner, there is no denying the fact that PTI is a political reality,” the PPP chairman stressed.

He emphasised that even if Imran was considered a “convicted felon or terrorist or whatever”, prisoners in a respectable society were entitled to their rights.

Bilawal said that although the PTI founder “tried to deny my family those rights”, he would not want to continue the cycle of “repeating the same mistakes” in vengeance.

“Khan sahib is a convict, he is in jail, but PTI is a political reality. Until PTI’s trust is restored in this system […] and they are able to play their role in the Parliament, the reset that is being discussed cannot take place in that manner,” he maintained.

The PPP chairman’s latest remarks come amid a growing debate over a “system reset” in the country. In July, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi stirred a political storm by calling for the creation of new administrative units, arguing that the current system of governance had “collapsed” and needed a “reset”.

On Nov 17, in a hard-hitting speech, Bilawal had asserted that the governance system had not collapsed, but was rather “made to collapse”.

In a similar vein, the Bhutto scion on Monday had called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system.

During Thursday’s address, Bilawal reiterated his call to regain the opposition’s “lost trust” in the system and for the government to undertake confidence-building measures (CBMs) to convince it that institutions such as the Parliament, the Election Commission of Pakistan, the courts, and the accountability system could be trusted again.

Responding to a query, Bilawal reiterated that the disputed reserved seats of the 2024 elections were a “low-hanging fruit” through which the opposition’s trust could be restored and that could serve as a CBM.

The PTI was deprived of its reserved seats in the 2024 elections following the revocation of its electoral symbol.

“Political parties will have to negotiate among themselves, or approach the court, or carry out reforms, so this gets done,” Bilawal suggested, adding that he was “not happy that another party” does not have its electoral symbol today.

“Personally, I believe they (PTI) should have received the reserved seats,” said Bilawal, whose PPP was one of the parties to challenge the Supreme Court ruling that declared PTI eligible for those seats.

However, in a deviation from that, Bilawal today said, “When PTI itself is saying that I am PTI, then we should listen to what they say and acknowledge it. However, that did not happen.”

Referring to the SC Constitutional Bench’s 2025 order that overturned the July 2024 ruling and consequently handed the seats to the coalition parties, Bilawal said, “That order, in my opinion, was also slightly extra.”

He said that even if his stance was that PTI should not get the reserved seats based on the argument that their leaders did not contest as PTI candidates, “how can those seats be given to me or the PML-N or JUI?”

Bilawal added: “According to that very argument, the argument on which you say that PTI cannot get [reserved seats] because they are not PTI, they are SIC, then I am not PTI either, JUI is not PTI, PML-N is not PTI.”

The PPP chairman stressed he was only raising this point because he believed if the opposition’s trust is to be restored, the government will have to think about such “goodwill gestures”.

‘All decisions have to be made in Parliament alone’

At the same time, the PPP chairman highlighted a similar “lack of trust” in the opposition on the government’s part and urged the opposition to view its role as a responsibility rather than a choice.

“They should sit in our finance committee in the Parliament. When the government presents the budget, [they should give their] input,” he said, adding that the opposition’s role was essential to tackling unemployment, inflation and poverty.

“But they haven’t been doing it for quite some time. They come for the judiciary, but there is also a committee for the judiciary, they do not sit in that either. They are not present in all committees of the Parliament,” Bilawal pointed out.

He called on the opposition to review if they benefitted from their boycott of such parliamentary initiatives, urging that it take part in the recently proposed electoral reforms committee.

“Until there are free and fair elections, until our country, our nation, all provinces, and all parties have confidence in this electoral system, there will be no trust, and the governments formed or referendums held as a result of that electoral system will lack legitimacy and strength,” Bilawal asserted.

The PPP chairman reiterated his stance that any “reset or reboot of our system” should be democratic and political, with all political stakeholders, including the opposition, made part of the conversation.

“If we want to make the Parliament functional, then all decisions have to be made in the Parliament alone,” he said, adding that decisions taken “outside the Parliament” would leave the system incapable of overcoming challenges.

Regarding a proposed “reset” in the country, Bilawal said even though he had not started the conversation, the discussion was welcomed.

“This country’s system has collapsed. I believe we should take this conversation forward: if the system has collapsed, why is that? How did it happen? Did it happen on its own? Because of political workers? Because of political parties?” he questioned.

“If you do not want to determine the responsibility for it, then don’t. But if you’re sick and I need to get you treated, then first I have to diagnose you to figure out what the illness is.”

He stressed that unless the stakeholders together identified why the system collapsed, there would be difficulties reviving it.

Recalling his Nov 17 remarks, Bilawal said the “system, meaning the 1973 Constitution, did not collapse on its own, it was made to collapse again and again”.

The PPP chairman called for a debate to identify the “diagnosis” with consensus, adding that a “reset should not be decided by a few former and current media anchors, media owners, and a few people belonging to business sectors, as they would not draw attention to people’s real issues”.

At one point, Bilawal remarked that nationalist parties in Sindh label PPP as “wafaaqparast” (pro-Centre) and those in Islamabad “affectionately call us “qoumparast” (nationalist), but his party was “Pakistan-parast and awaamparast”.

‘You can’t have a hard state with thin skin’

The Bhutto scion further said, “This country should have enough courage that we can listen to the truth and tolerate each other’s differences of opinion.”

He termed the reactions to his Nov 17 press conference as “inappropriate”, contending that there were patriotic Pakistanis on both sides of an argument even if they had differing opinions.

Bilawal continued: “If anyone thinks that we can be silenced through such cheap tactics, that is not possible.

“It is now said these days that ‘Pakistan is a hard state’. For Pakistan to be that, the hard state should have thick skin. You can’t have a hard state with thin skin.”

Responding to a question, Bilawal said he not only condemned the recent actions against the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl chief during his stay in Lahore, but also termed them “incomprehensible”.

“If you will take such revengeful actions even against Maulana Fazlur Rehman, then do you expect them to clap for you or praise you?” he remarked.

The PPP chairman argued that as an opposition member, it was Fazl’s “patriotic duty” to criticise the government. “We should have a thick skin and absorb that criticism,” he said, adding that any suggestion in it that could lead to better decisions should be incorporated.

‘Non-existent press freedom’

During his address, the PPP chairman also highlighted the importance of a free press, adding that he wanted to restore the “power” previously held by press clubs across the country.

“With your voice, your columns, you used to make and topple governments,” the Bhutto scion remarked.

“I don’t want to topple any government, nor do I want to form another one. But I believe your role is to hold up a mirror to those sitting in power,” he added.

Bilawal said he was not denying “mistakes” made by him over time, insisting that his party’s intention was not to weaken the press.

He referred to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca), which was amended in January 2025 despite countrywide protests by journalists’ bodies.

He remarked that regardless of the PPP’s intention, the country had now arrived at a point where press freedom was non-existent.

The PPP chairman noted that if the media was given space only to regurgitate what those in power talked about among themselves, then issues related to economic crises and difficulties faced by the people at the grassroots level would not come to the forefront.

‘27th Amendment a success but judicial system lacks trust’

Bilawal also elaborated on his earlier remarks about the 26th and 27th Constitutional Amendments, insisting that an impression was being given as if he was backing away from them or criticising them.

In his Nov 17 remark, the PPP chairman, who had strongly advocated for the amendments at the time of their passage, had said the 27th Amendment was “passed neither through political consensus nor bilateral agreement; it was passed with brute majority”.

He had also questioned the current status of the judiciary, particularly in the wake of the 27th Amendment, noting that resignations of senior judges followed the legislation.

The next day, the PPP chairman clarified that he was “not disowning” the 27th Amendment, but rather noting that it did not enjoy the same “unanimous consensus” as the 18th Amendment and the 1973 Constitution.

“It’s not black and white,” Bilawal said today, stressing that the 1973 Constitution and the 18th Amendment were passed through mutual consensus.

He defended that the 26th Amendment was passed with as much consensus as could be developed and declared the passage of the 27th Amendment with a two-thirds majority a “success”.

“But, at the same time, I believe we cannot ignore the fact today that our opposition does not have confidence in this judicial system,” Bilawal stated, adding that judges and lawyers he interacts with are also “not comfortable” with the current status of the judiciary.

“Does this mean I am saying we should tear it up? No. I am merely asking what steps we can take, how can dialogue be held with all stakeholders, so that we can restore that lost trust?”

The PPP chairman clarified that while an attempt was made to make his “brute majority” remarks on the 27th Amendment controversial, as if he had meant force or used the word “brutal”, he had simply referred to the two-thirds majority that the legislation had.

‘Accountability system used solely for political opponents’

During his address, the PPP chairman also doubled down on his criticism of the country’s accountability system, asserting that its structure was “based on political victimisation”

“Unfortunately, no matter how big the claims the governments came in with, the more emphasis they placed on eradicating corruption, the more corruption there has been,” he remarked.

Bilawal contended that despite strong rhetoric by governments on ending corruption, they failed to do so as the accountability system was “used solely against political opponents”.

The PPP chairman regretted that ongoing discussions in the Parliament, the federal cabinet, seminars, or even television talk shows did not pay attention to the fundamental issues faced by the public.

“People are distressed about managing two square meals. They’re worried whether they should educate their children or arrange medicines for their elders,” he said.

Bilawal noted there was “restlessness and distress” among Pakistan’s youth, who faced unemployment and, even if employed, their salaries were spent on just commuting to and from work.

“If we truly want this system to serve the public, want our country to be capable of facing every problem, whether they are economic hardships or foreign difficulties, then we will have to take steps as soon as possible so we can establish unity, political stability, and restore trust in all institutions,” he stated.

articles.title: NDC alleges assassination attempt on Kano TikToker, Maryam Golden
articles.summary:
From Desmond Mgboh, Kano

The New Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential/Gubernatorial Campaign Council in Kano State has alleged an assassination attempt on Miss Maryam Golden, a TikToker and NDC stalwart.

In a press release signed by its Director General, Gwani Shehu Wada Sagagi, the council said the incident occurred on the evening of Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at about 9:00 p.m. at the residence of the victim at Rimin Kebe Quarters, Kano.

According to the statement, four masked men allegedly visited the house where Maryam Golden resides with her parents, and attacked her with dangerous weapons, inflicting severe injuries on several parts of her body.

The council described the attack as shocking and disgusting, and claimed it bore semblance with sponsored terrorism by a section of the political elite who were allegedly unhappy with her eloquence and massive followership on social media.

It further alleged that the attack was a clear message by their opponent to silence the opposition by encouraging violence as a means of resolving political differences rather than the ballot.

The statement described the victim as a simple, decent and law-abiding citizen who, in the exercise of her constitutional right to free speech and political association, decided to belong to the NDC and propagate Kwankwasiyya ideals.

It warned that such an approach to politics would not augur well for political actors in the state, adding that no political group has a monopoly of violence, and that the council would not hesitate to call on its supporters to defend themselves whenever attacked by hoodlums or criminals.

The council called on security agencies in the state to investigate the incident with a view to apprehending the culprits and their sponsors and subjecting them to due process of law.

articles.title: No rift with my predecessor – Gov Umo Eno
articles.summary:
Akwa Ibom state governor pastor Umo has dispelled rumours of altercation between him and his predecessor Mr Udom Emmanuel saying his relationship with the former governor is intact and in good mode .

Recall that there is public speculation that pastor Umo Eno is not in terms with Udom Emmanuel who facilitated his emergence as governor of the state in 2023 .

Speaking during local government campaign in Onna council area where Mr Udom Emmanuel comes from, pastor Umo Eno disabused the mind of the people declaring that there is no rift between them and reaffirmed his enduring political relationship with Udom Emmanuel and the people of Onna Local Government Area.

Eno described Onna the home of Mr Udom Emmanuel as his second home and expressed profound appreciation to the former governor as his political father and his wife, Deaconess Martha Emmanuel as well as the entire Onna people for discovering, nurturing and supporting his political journey, which culminated in his emergence as Governor of Akwa Ibom State in 2023.

Eno challenged those spreading rumours of discord to disregard such narratives, insisting that he has remained committed to the interests of Onna and has justified the confidence reposed in him by Udom Emmanuel through political appointments, infrastructural developments and inclusive governance.

Eno defended his decision to defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC) adding that it was the best political decision for the overall interest of Akwa Ibom State.

He reminded the critics to consider where the state would have been if he had failed to make the move at the appropriate time.

Drawing inspiration from the biblical sons of Issachar, who understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do, Governor Eno said political leaders must be sensitive to changing realities and make decisions in the best interest of their people.

“You must understand the direction of the wind

” My decision to join the APC was partly informed by the need to support Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio being an indigene of Akwa Ibom State to occupy such an influential national position should be a source of collective pride and political advantage for the state

” This administration constructed 64 kilometres of roads, 19 Compassionate Homes, a health centre and other development initiatives in Onna local government as a mark of royalty to my predecessor”

He however, promised additional intervention projects in the area and announced the construction of another health centre in the area.

Eno directed that the Akwa Ibom State University Teaching Hospital be properly furnished, equipped and staffed to fulfil its mandate, particularly in supporting the clinical training of medical students of the university.

Governor Eno commended the Chairman of Onna Local Government Area, Hon. Kufre Umoren, for his responsible leadership and urged party faithful to intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the forthcoming elections.

He called on APC supporters to take the party’s message to every household and encouraged eligible citizens who were yet to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) to do so without delay.

Earlier, the Deputy Governor, Senator Akon Eyakenyi, commended the wife of the immediate past Governor, Deaconess Martha Udom Emmanuel, for her significant role in mobilising support for Governor Umo Eno’s emergence in the 2023 governorship election.

 

 

The post No rift with my predecessor – Gov Umo Eno appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: NUJ FCT, NBSA partner to launch Rafat Salami blood donation drive
articles.summary:
The Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), FCT Council, has partnered with the National Blood Service Agency (NBSA) to launch a voluntary blood donation drive in honour of late Comrade Rafat Salami, a journalist and committed blood donor.

 

Tagged the Rafat Salami Voluntary Blood Donation Drive, the initiative was aimed at sustaining her legacy of service and sacrifice, while promoting voluntary blood donation and public awareness of its life-saving importance.

 

The partnership was sealed on Thursday during a courtesy visit by a delegation of the NUJ FCT Council to the NBSA. The partnership marked a significant step in honouring Rafat Salami’s legacy, with journalists in Abuja committing to remember her each December 9 through an act she championed in her lifetime which was giving blood to save lives.

 

The visit, led by Felix Ojo on behalf of the Council Chairman, Comrade Grace Ike, culminated in a shared commitment to encourage journalists to move beyond reporting blood donation campaigns to actively participating in them.

 

“We are immortalising the legacy of donor champion, late Comrade Rafat Salami, who lived a life of sacrifice and responsibility,” Ojo said.

 

He said the Council was committed to encouraging its members to donate blood voluntarily, raise public awareness and advocate for regular blood donation, while supporting the NBSA’s mandate as part of the media’s social responsibility to promote good initiatives and good governance.

 

The Media Cell for Safe Blood, a collaborative platform established by the International Society of Media in Public Health (ISMPH) in partnership with the NBSA, will also participate in the initiative, particularly in public awareness and advocacy.

 

As part of the partnership, the NUJ FCT Council announced that December 9 would be dedicated annually in Abuja to commemorating the initiative, making it a permanent event on the Council’s calendar.

 

Receiving the delegation, the Director of Blood Services, Dr. Sani Abubakar, welcomed the NUJ’s commitment to voluntary blood donation, describing it as a positive development for the agency and the country’s blood donation campaign.

 

“Rafat Salami was a consistent donor and advocate. It is sad we lost her,” Abubakar said. “It is a good thing that the NUJ wants to immortalise her by her legacy.”

 

He said the NBSA was open to collaboration, explaining that its mandate was to regulate and coordinate the provision of safe blood across Nigeria.

 

Abubakar disclosed that activities marking the National Blood Donation Day would begin on December 8, with a week-long advocacy campaign to promote voluntary blood donation, assuring the NUJ of adequate blood bank facilities for its members.

 

“We are happy to have the NUJ supporting our work, and we will adopt the initiative as part of our annual event every December,” he said.

 

He added that while the NBSA would provide technical and material support, the NUJ FCT Council should take full ownership of the event’s sponsorship to ensure a sense of pride and commitment.

 

 

 

The post NUJ FCT, NBSA partner to launch Rafat Salami blood donation drive appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: Sinach blends Afrobeats, gospel in new single ‘Dis One’
articles.summary:
Nigerian gospel singer and songwriter Sinach has released a new single titled ‘Dis One’, combining Afrobeats rhythms with gospel melodies to explore themes of gratitude, faith and divine intervention.

Released on Friday, November 27, 2026, the song serves as the title track of her forthcoming album, which centres on thanksgiving, praise and the faithfulness of God.

According to the release announcement, the composition was inspired by Ephesians 3:20, a biblical passage that speaks about God’s ability to accomplish more than people can ask or imagine.

The single continues Sinach’s approach to songwriting, which frequently draws on biblical teachings and expressions of Christian faith while incorporating musical elements intended to encourage collective worship.

With ‘Dis One’, Sinach incorporates Afrobeats-inspired rhythms into a gospel composition built around an accessible message of thanksgiving.

The combination reflects the increasingly fluid relationship between contemporary African popular music and gospel, as Christian recording artistes explore different musical styles while retaining the spiritual foundations of their work.

The use of Nigerian Pidgin English in ‘Dis One’ is particularly significant in this regard. The language, widely spoken across Nigeria and parts of West Africa, gives the song a distinctly local identity while communicating a theme that extends beyond geographical boundaries.

Rather than relying on elaborate expressions of worship, the central refrain draws on everyday language, making the song’s message accessible to listeners familiar with the expression.

The release also invites audiences to reflect on their personal experiences and share testimonies of moments they consider evidence of God’s faithfulness.

Sinach is widely recognised for her contributions to contemporary Christian music, particularly through compositions such as ‘Way Maker’ and ‘I Know Who I Am’.

Her songwriting has frequently explored themes of faith, spiritual identity, hope and trust in God, with several of her compositions becoming familiar features of Christian worship in Nigeria and internationally.

‘Way Maker’, in particular, has been performed by numerous gospel and contemporary Christian musicians around the world, contributing to the international visibility of Nigerian gospel music.

The release of ‘Dis One’ adds another thanksgiving-focused composition to her catalogue while placing greater emphasis on Nigerian linguistic and musical influences.

Its combination of contemporary African rhythms and Christian worship themes also illustrates how gospel musicians can draw from their cultural environments without departing from the religious messages that define their work.

As the title single from Sinach’s forthcoming album, ‘Dis One’ offers an indication of the thematic direction of the project.

The album is expected to explore thanksgiving, praise and reflections on God’s faithfulness, with the lead single establishing gratitude as a central element of the project.

However, details regarding the album’s official release date, complete tracklist, production credits and possible collaborations were not disclosed in the announcement.

The single arrives as Nigerian gospel music continues to develop across multiple genres, with artistes incorporating elements of Afrobeats, traditional African music and contemporary worship into their recordings.

For Sinach, ‘Dis One’ continues her exploration of faith through music, this time using an expression rooted in everyday Nigerian conversation to convey a message of thanksgiving.

Through the release, the singer encourages listeners to consider their own experiences of answered prayers, unexpected opportunities, and personal breakthroughs, turning individual reflections into expressions of collective praise.

The post Sinach blends Afrobeats, gospel in new single ‘Dis One’ appeared first on The Sun Nigeria.

articles.title: FG launches free maternal health insurance in Imo
articles.summary:
From Stanley Uzoaru, Owerri

The Federal Government has launched the Expanding Maternal and Child Health Insurance Initiative, also known as “Mama Pikin”, in Imo State, with a target of 20,000 enrolments for vulnerable women, children and members of their households.

The nationwide launch, held in Imo State on Wednesday, November 26, 2026, was attended by over 500 pregnant women.

The Honourable Minister of Health and Social Welfare, professor Muhammad Ali Pate in his keynote address at the occasion, said the vision of the government is clear ” every woman should be able to seek care in time, receive the care she needs and bring her child safely into the world without cost standing between her and help”.

He recalled that at the 2024 Joint Annual Review, he announced that any vulnerable woman who requires a caesarean section would receive it free of charge.

Since then, he said, the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) has implemented the Financial Access to Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care initiative, known as CEmONC. The programme now operates in more than 270 hospitals across every state in Nigeria and has provided care to more than 100,000 women and newborns.

The Minister said the new initiative goes beyond emergency response. He explained that It will help women connect with the health system earlier, before an emergency, and throughout pregnancy and childbirth.

Ali said the initiative is part of the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and the Health Sector Strategic Blueprint 2023-2027, which seeks to save lives, reduce physical and financial pain, and produce health for all Nigerians.

According to him, over the past three years, N249.6 billion has been disbursed to the Basic Health Care Provision Fund nationwide to strengthen care, improve financial protection and support access for the most vulnerable.

He said Imo has begun work under MAMII, the Maternal and Neonatal Mortality Reduction Innovation Initiative, including the launch at Umuohiagu Health Centre in Ngor Okpala and the establishment of a state taskforce.

He commended the Imo State Government as an excellent partner, citing the June MoU to upgrade General Hospital, Okigwe, into a Federal Medical Centre, following the approval to convert the Federal Medical Centre, Owerri, into a university teaching hospital.

The Minister stressed that enrolment is a beginning, not the finish line. He said families must be able to use their coverage when they need care, women must know where to go, and facilities must be ready to provide services.

He charged the Imo State Government, the Imo State Health Insurance Agency, NHIA, partners and frontline teams to hold themselves to that standard.

Earlier, in his opening remarks, the Director-General of National Health Insurance Agency (NHIA) said the initiative marks a shift from responding to complications when they occur to proactively protecting women and their families against financial risks.

He said the Kano State Health Insurance Agency will lead implementation in Kano, while NHIA will work with the Imo State Government to deliver the initiative in Imo.

Ohiri explained that the programme will track who enrolls and whether they can use their coverage when they need care, so that enrolment translates into lower out-of-pocket spending for families.à

The Minister formally launched the Expanding Maternal and Child Health Insurance Initiative in Imo State, saying what is learned in Imo will help improve how the promise works for families across the country.

Governor Hope Uzodimma present at the event said the initiative is one of President Ahmed Tinubu’s contribution towards healthcare in the country and urged that he is reelected a second time to complete all his laudable projects not only in health but other sectors.

articles.title: MAAUN Niger pioneered Nursing Education revolution in northern Nigeria – Prof. Gwarzo
articles.summary:
The President of the MAAUN Group of Universities, Professor Adamu Abubakar Gwarzo, has highlighted the significant contributions of Maryam Abacha American University of Niger (MAAUN Niger) to the growth and development of Bachelor of Nursing Science education in Northern Nigeria.

Professor Gwarzo made this known on Thursday in Kaduna at the launch of a book titled “A Compendium for the Struggle for the Establishment of Bachelor of Nursing Science Degree Programme in Northern Nigeria,” authored by Dr. Muhammad Jumare.

Professor Gwarzo, who served as the Chief Launcher at the event, demonstrated his support for the documentation of the history by launching the book with a donation of ₦10 million.

Recounting the challenges encountered in establishing the Department of Nursing Sciences at MAAUN Niger, Professor Gwarzo said the journey was difficult but ultimately rewarding, as the initiative helped open new opportunities for nursing diploma holders to obtain university degrees.

“We faced numerous challenges while establishing the Department of Nursing Sciences at MAAUN Niger. However, through consistency and determination, we were able to make it a reality. That initiative opened the door for many diploma holders in nursing to acquire university degrees.

“When we established the department, there were only a few graduates of Bachelor of Nursing Science in the region. Today, many of our graduates have risen to directorate positions across Northern Nigeria, and they are a testament to the impact of MAAUN Niger.

“We came at a time when Ahmadu Bello University (ABU), Zaria, was virtually the only institution offering a Bachelor of Nursing Science programme in the region. Today, the story has changed significantly.

“Many of our graduates are now working in countries such as Canada, the United Kingdom and Belgium, while more than 2,000 are practising in Saudi Arabia. This is a proud moment for us and a testament to the role MAAUN Niger has played in advancing nursing education,” he stated.

Professor Gwarzo further commended the author, Dr. Muhammad Jumare, for his remarkable efforts in documenting the struggles and milestones that led to the establishment of Bachelor of Nursing Science programmes in Northern Nigeria.

He emphasised that documenting such historical experiences was important to preserve institutional memories, recognise the contributions of those who pioneered the initiative and inspire younger generations to appreciate the sacrifices behind the development of nursing education in the region.

The event was attended by the Deputy Governor of Kaduna State, Dr. Hadiza Sabuwa Balarabe, alongside other distinguished personalities from the education, health and public sectors.

articles.title: EPL: Pogba urges Man Utd to abandon past glory, follow Arsenal’s example
articles.summary:
Former Manchester United midfielder, Paul Pogba, has urged the club to stop dwelling on its past achievements and instead learn from Arsenal’s gradual return to the top of English football.

Pogba said Manchester United must give their new manager, Mauricio Pochettino, enough time to rebuild the team rather than expect immediate success.

The former France international made the remarks during an interview with talkSPORT following United’s 2-2 draw against Sporting CP in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday.

He expressed support for Pochettino, describing him as a great manager, and called on the club’s management, players and supporters to give him the necessary time to implement his ideas.

“I’m happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he is a great manager,” Pogba said.

“Everybody needs to give time to the manager to do his things.”

He pointed to Arsenal’s rebuilding process under Mikel Arteta as an example Manchester United should follow, noting that the North London club was allowed to develop gradually before returning to the top.

Pogba also said United needed to address internal problems and ensure that everyone at the club worked towards the same objective.

“Arsenal made their own way back to the top and that is all I think Manchester United need. We need to stop talking about Manchester United as if they are the team they were back then,” he added.

United have struggled in the Premier League this season, collecting eight points from 11 matches and sitting in the relegation zone.

Their poor run led to the departure of Michael Carrick and the appointment of Pochettino.

articles.title: 2027: Imo APC warns Wike against political interference in state
articles.summary:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Imo State has warned Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to stay away from the state, accusing him of attempting to interfere in its political affairs ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The party vowed to resist any attempt to import what it described as Wike’s controversial political tactics into Imo, insisting that the state was not available for political manipulation.

In a statement yesterday, the state Publicity Secretary, Onwuasoanya Jones, reacted to reports that Wike had concluded arrangements to secure electoral victories for President Bola Tinubu and the APC in the forthcoming elections, while offering to undertake additional political assignments for the President, including delivering other states.

The Imo APC dismissed the minister’s claims, saying he should not assume that his political activities could determine the party’s electoral fortunes in different states. It also faulted his reported suggestion that Imo and another APC-controlled state had political challenges requiring his intervention.

“We would have ignored the politically displaced errand boy, like we always do, but for the fact that we deem this particular statement of his a direct affront on the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the electoral integrity of our dear party, the APC,” the statement said.

The party accused Wike of attempting to portray Tinubu as politically dependent on individuals outside the APC to win elections, insisting that it had its own grassroots support and political structure.

It also criticised the minister’s reported claim that he had already secured victory for the APC in the FCT and Rivers State, describing such declarations weeks before the elections as disrespectful to democratic principles and the electorate.

“Our party, the All Progressives Congress, has immense regard for the Nigerian people and would not encourage actions and utterances that tend to cast the Nigerian electorate as irrelevant in the determination of their political future,” the statement added.

The Imo APC further accused Wike of leveraging the party’s political goodwill to sustain his relevance while allegedly making disparaging remarks about some of its leaders. It challenged him to demonstrate his political influence by campaigning for his own party, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), instead of claiming to deliver APC victories.

The party maintained that its political activities in Imo were progressing smoothly, expressing confidence in its preparations for the 2027 elections and its mobilisation efforts across the state ahead of the January 16 and February 6, 2027, polls.

It also alleged that Wike had deployed political associates and emissaries to Imo with financial inducements to create divisions within the APC, although it did not provide specific details or evidence to substantiate the allegation.

Describing the alleged moves as attempts to introduce godfatherism, political intimidation and electoral manipulation into the state, the party said it had warned those reportedly involved against such activities.

articles.title: Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports
articles.summary:
Loud explosions rock Riyadh as Houthis attack Saudi ports

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 21:13

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman expected to travel to the US next month for G-20 in first trip since start of war

This aerial photograph shows a view of the Riyadh skyline on 23 November 2026

Off

Fresh explosions rocked Riyadh on Wednesday as Yemen's Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan, as the kingdom’s deterrence and defensive capabilities continue to be challenged.

The Houthis said that both strikes on the ports “resulted in damage” while the Saudi-led coalition acknowledged that a projectile hit the port of Jazan, resulting in minor damage and no casualties.

The port strikes followed an attack on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia’s largest refinery. Argus Media, which covers commodity markets, said the Houthis landed two successful blows on the facility, one at the refinery and one at the export terminal. The Houthis say they bombed Ras Tanura as retaliation for the Saudi attack on the port of Hodeidah controlled by the group.

Saudi Arabia is shooting down the majority of Houthi missiles and drones fired at it, Arab and Western officials tell Middle East Eye, but it has failed to protect key assets like energy facilities, financial centres and airports.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has tried to rally the US and regional states to his side. Egypt, Pakistan, Turkey and Syria have all sent or committed to delivering military support to Saudi Arabia, but with the exception of Syria - which has sent drone operators - the assistance is defensive.

The Crown Prince met US Central Command chief admiral Brad Cooper, the commander of forces in the Middle East, last week. MEE first reported the planned meeting, which was the third since fighting with the Houthis resumed in July.

The US, Saudi Arabia's top military supplier, however has not publicly committed additional support to the kingdom, although it has troops and advisers inside the country.

Iran tensions simmer

Semafor reported on Wednesday that Mohammed bin Salman will travel to the US next month for the G-20 summit in Miami. Diplomats have speculated for months whether the de facto leader of Saudi Arabia would leave the kingdom amid Houthi strikes and the chances of a new US-Israeli attack on Iran.

'Turn on the weapons spigot': Saudi Arabia asks partners for gear to deter Houthis

Read More »

Tensions between the US and Iran have been simmering for months, with the two sides exchanging blows in the Strait of Hormuz and at some land targets. The US has conducted strikes on Iran’s mainland while Tehran has responded with attacks on US military sites in Kuwait and Bahrain.

Iran said on Wednesday that an oil tanker hit a naval mine and caught fire in a "restricted zone" in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the semi-official Fars news agency.

Brent, the international oil benchmark, was up 2.5 percent on Wednesday, trading at $84 per barrel.

The Trump administration says that it is not interested in resuming the war on Iran for now, and instead wants to use economic means to collapse the government, mainly through a blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran has been hit by debilitating inflation, although regional officials who have traveled to the capital have reported busy restaurants and a sense of calm. Fars said on Wednesday that a substantial shipment of dollar banknotes had entered Iran from a neighbouring country.

articles.title: US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year
articles.summary:
US ambassador to Israel undercuts Trump's announcement that aid to Israel will end this year

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 18:44

The president's abrupt announcement came on the morning of the midterm elections earlier this month

Students carry placards depicting US President Donald Trump and Israel's caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu carrying guns, as they march during a general strike over rising living costs and military spending called by the CGIL trade union, in Milan, Italy, on 20 November 2026 (Claudia Greco/Reuters)

Off

US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee has undercut US President Donald Trump's assertion earlier this month that he "won't be paying Israel" by the end of this year.

Huckabee, the former governor of Arkansas who is an evangelical pastor and a staunch Zionist - by his own description - said on Tuesday at a conference in Tel Aviv that he's "not certain that there will be a cessation on an abrupt basis by the end of this year". 

That's because Washington currently gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028.

The package also includes $3.3bn in foreign military financing and $500m in cooperative missile defence programmes.

In May, the Israeli defence ministry said that the two sides had begun formal talks to replace the current memorandum, with discussions focusing on joint investment in research, development and weapons production.

The suggested framework was to move the relationship from aid to a more reciprocal partnership. 

The Congressional Research Service, a non-partisan research body that advises the US Congress, further confirmed this in a June report that US and Israeli officials were discussing a possible shift after 2028 away from direct military aid and towards joint programmes.

Israel, a full-scale partner

In July, the Republican-controlled House of Representatives narrowly passed a $1.5 trillion budget for the US Department of War, and the bill included a controversial provision that would permanently integrate US and Israeli military tech advancements in a way that would - as Netanyahu put it - turn Israel from a foreign aid recipient to a full-scale partner. 

Future presidents would not be able to simply withdraw from such a project. 

Kushner says Israel is becoming a 'pariah' as his Board of Peace plans stall

Read More »

The National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) is must-pass legislation, as it is needed to fund all of the Pentagon's operations in the year to come. The Senate will have to consider it soon.

But emboldened by the incoming Democratic majority in January, a dozen Democrats, led by Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen, are seeking to remove the provisions related to Section 219, which establishes the "United States–Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative".

The project would identify jointly developed or Israeli-origin technologies for potential integration into US systems; ensure collaborative research initiatives involving government, private sector and academic institutions in both countries protect "sensitive technology"; and ultimately align military efforts with the Department of War that include the Irregular Warfare Technical Support Directorate, the Defense Innovation Unit, the Missile Defense Agency and the United States Space Command, among others. 

Huckabee said at the Institute for National Security Studies conference on Tuesday that American lives are saved "every day" because "we pick up intelligence from our partners in Israel". 

Military ties continue

On 3 November, Trump said that his administration will not give its yearly military aid to Israel starting next year, because of a prior understanding he made with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. 

Trump added that weapon sales and other forms of military cooperation would continue. 

Speaking on Fox News, the president said that the two had agreed months ago to end the military aid since Israel no longer needed it.

Britain must stand firm against Nusseibeh's UN candidacy

Read More »

“Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4bn a year, and we made a deal months ago that we're stopping,” Trump said.

“We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel. Now we'll help Israel if they need it,” he added.

Trump said Israel would be able to purchase weapons from the United States and other countries, suggesting that the change would affect the form of assistance rather than bring an end to military ties.

"They can buy whatever they want. They can buy whatever they want. So can Europe. We make the greatest weapons in the world," he said.

The comments came as Republican lawmakers and establishment Democrats running for Congress - as well as hundreds of statewide races - faced growing electoral pressure over support for Israel ahead of the midterm elections.

And indeed, the so-called blue tsunami, led by an energised progressive Democratic movement that wants to curb US aid to Israel, washed over Capitol Hill and state legislatures, including several governorships.

articles.title: The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war
articles.summary:
The gold-filled mountains of Chad that hold the key to Libya's crisis and Sudan's war

Submitted by
MEE correspondent
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 14:23

A mining dispute in a town of a few thousand people tucked away in the remote roof of the Sahara has become entangled with an arms corridor sustaining one of the world’s deadliest wars

The Tibesti mountains run through northern Chad into southern Libya, and are home to the Tubu people (MEE)

Off

Deep inside the Tibesti mountains of northern Chad, in the central Sahara, the town of Miski sits surrounded by a succession of never-ending wadis. 

A couple of families live at the top of each of these valleys and in August, when the rainy season comes, the wadis become a river that washes through the mountains. When the rains go, the valleys become green and camels feed on them.

A remote volcanic range characterised by rugged, bare rock, rivers of lava and volcanoes that climb to 3,000 metres, the Tibesti, which runs through northern Chad across the border into southern Libya, is sometimes called the roof of the Sahara. 

These mountains are home to the Tubu, an indigenous community whose territory also includes a part of southern Libya, northern Niger and northwestern Sudan.

And the valleys that surround the town of Miski contain vast deposits of a precious metal that throughout human history has been prized almost above anything else: gold. 

The mountains, too, are filled with antimony, a toxic heavy metal that is putting the ecosystem of this indigenous community at severe risk and is also exported in great quantities. 

For decades, the gold that sits in this remote place has been one of the drivers of armed conflict between the Tubu and the Libyan, then Chadian states. 

Now, the Tubu find themselves caught up in a web of warfare and illicit trade that stretches out from Chad into Libya, Sudan and over the sea to the United Arab Emirates, from where arms and supplies are flown to proxy armies, militias and paramilitaries. 

On 14 October, armed clashes broke out in Miski.

The day after fighting began, the Chadian army’s general staff accused Miski’s self-defence committee - a local armed group descended from the Tubu institution of village guardianship - of breaking a peace agreement struck between them and the army last year by attacking the National Brigade for the Control of Mining Activities.

The army gave the Tubu group an ultimatum: lay down your arms at once or be treated as rebels. In response, the committee accused the brigade of firing first and of opening new mining fronts in grazing lands, in violation of the Bardai peace accord signed last year.

The gold ends up in Dubai…'yet we do not have a single clinic in Miski or a single paved road in the whole of the Tibesti' 

- Tubu commander

One Tubu commander in Miski told Middle East Eye that last year Chad had exported over $1bn worth of gold and more than 15,000 tonnes of antimony, all sourced from the Tibesti mountains.

Almost all this gold ends up in the UAE, in the gold market of Dubai.

“And yet we do not have a single clinic in Miski or a single paved road in the whole of the Tibesti,” the commander said. “We won’t let this continue.”

Since the armed clashes broke out in October, the Chadian army has moved considerable numbers of troops and armoured vehicles into the Tibesti.  

The situation on the ground, according to one Chadian army officer who spoke to MEE, is difficult for government troops. “We are fighting the mines and the mountains in Miski,” he said.

This fighting has not stopped: scores of people have died in the clashes and the Chadian army has conducted multiple drone strikes across the mountain range.

Weapons corridor

Miski’s uprising appears, on the surface, to be a local fight over gold - and in a large part, it is. 

But it is unfolding inside a region that has become one of the most consequential, least scrutinised arms corridors in Africa: a route that, according to United Nations investigators and extensive reporting from Middle East Eye, has carried weapons, fuel and fighters from the UAE through Libya and Chad to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan. 

How the UAE continued supporting Sudan's RSF through Haftar and Libya

Read More »

These weapons are part of a network of arms and mercenaries that spans swathes of north and central Africa, utilised not just in Sudan but by organised criminal groups and armed entities across the Sahel.   

Between October 2024 and the end of 2025, according to a UN Panel of Experts report, heavy cargo aircraft made 458 flights between military airports in the UAE or the Emirati base at Bosaso in the breakaway Somali region of Puntland and eastern Libya.  

Some 239 of these landed at Kufra, a town about 300km from the Sudan border that was transformed, in the months before the RSF took el-Fasher in October 2025, into a fortified logistics hub complete with new hangars and scheduled flights. 

Separately, as reported by MEE and confirmed by UN experts, the UAE was using Amdjarass, in eastern Chad, to land cargo planes.

Senior Egyptian army sources told MEE earlier this year that the Emiratis have a military operations room inside Amdjarass airport to coordinate with the RSF.

Just over 100km from the border with Darfur, the vast western region of Sudan controlled by the RSF, Amdjarass is a Zaghawa-dominated town that is the home region of Chad’s president, Mahamat Idriss Deby, and the site of a lavish state infrastructure programme that residents of Tibesti, 1,300km away and without a single paved road or a functioning hospital between them, have started to openly resent.

Abu Dhabi continues to deny supplying the Rapid Support Forces.

Haftar’s expanding footprint

In November 2025, Chad and the UAE-backed Haftar family’s Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), de facto commanded by Khalifa Haftar’s son Saddam, formed a joint border force covering roughly 1,050km of shared frontier.

The Haftars are not just in control of eastern Libya: leaked details of US adviser Massad Boulos’s plan to unify Libya propose Saddam Haftar as president of a government that would continue to be led by Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah. 

Chad’s government has two reasons to want this partnership, and they reinforce each other. 

One is logistical: Chad and Haftar can cement their relationship in the eastern Libyan corridor that carries Emirati arms to the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan. 

The other is that a joint border force hems in the Tubu, who have supplied the armed resistance to Mahamat Deby’s government and to Haftar’s forces alike. 

Jalel Harchaoui, an analyst focusing on Libya and political economy, told Middle East Eye that when the deal was initially struck, the Tubu were not part of the thinking.

The only connection in the remote area - Starlink (MEE)

“It was to ensure better security along the route between Chad and Libya, especially with the passage via Ma’tan as-Sarra in Libya down through Chad to Amdjarass and then on to Darfur,” he said.

This “security problem” included armed groups attacking the convoys headed to Darfur to supply the RSF, Harchaoui said. There was also the need to build further cooperation between Emirati allies who were not natural bedfellows.

“Saddam Haftar and Mahamat Deby don’t get along, so there was a need to please the UAE by doing a joint force. And the agreement was never that the joint force would be pushed to the west, it was really to cover the northeastern corner of Chad,” Harchaoui said.

That changed earlier this year, when Saddam Haftar “ran into trouble” with armed Tubu groups like the Southern Liberation Operations Room (Slor), which is led by Mohamed Wardougou, a Libyan Tubu, and often hides out in northern Niger.

Haftar asked Chad to move forces to the west, arguing correctly, according to Harchaoui, “that Wardougou’s activism served as a shot in the arm for the anti-Deby Chadian group Front for Change and Concord in Chad (Fact) in northern Niger”.

History of revolt

This move played into the Tubu’s long record of rising up against the central governments of Chad, going back to the country’s independence from France in 1960. 

Their most recent armed revolt, in April 2021, culminated in the death on the front line of President Idriss Deby Itno, who had decided at the age of 68 to command his forces in person. His son Mahamat succeeded him.

In Libya too, the Tubu rose against Muammar Gaddafi, and after his fall in 2011, they held sway over vast stretches of southern Libya until 2021, when Haftar’s forces pushed into the areas they had controlled. The containment effort carries a human cost well beyond Tibesti. 

In Libya, Tubu communities describe a steady tightening around their citizenship, with human rights researchers long having flagged discriminatory practices such as treating the Tubu as second-class citizens and stopping them from obtaining passports and IDs. 

'We do not want to be part of a bigger game… We just want peace and justice and foremost, transparency in mining and the development of our region'

- Tubu defence committee member

On 14 October, the same day gunfire broke out in Miski, Libya’s attorney general in Tripoli said he was prepared to strip the 28,000 families registered at Murzuq, in the Fezzan region of southwest Libya, of their Libyan nationality, citing alleged forgery. 

Because the overwhelming majority of Libya’s Tubu are registered through that one civil registry, the announcement reads as an existential threat: if carried through, most of Libya’s Tubu would become stateless.

On the border between Libya and Niger, Wardougou’s Slor group has fought a running battle with Haftar’s forces, using northern Niger as a rear base. The Slor’s declared aim is to remove Haftar’s men from southern Libya.

In July, photographs circulated online showing Chadian soldiers at Libya’s Wigh airbase, near the Nigerien border - evidence, the group’s leadership says, that Chad is fighting on Haftar’s behalf. 

On 20 October, the LAAF arrested a former Chadian minister and senior opposition figure, Hassan Soukaya, as he tried to cross from Libya into Niger, and handed him to the Chadian army.

Days later, Niger’s government publicly accused the Chadian military, with alleged French support, of carrying out a drone strike on 24 October near the Salvador Pass that killed two civilians. The attack was reportedly meant to target Slor positions in Libya, but hit Nigerien territory by accident.

The UAE-Israel desert axis

On 19 October, Israel’s second-ever ambassador to Chad landed in N’Djamena to present her credentials to Deby.

Since taking power after his father’s death in 2021, Deby has made a point of binding Chad ever closer to the UAE and Israel: diplomatic relations with Israel were restored in 2022, and the first Israeli ambassador in more than half a century - since Chad broke off ties in 1972 - was received shortly afterwards. Despite this, in November 2023, Chad recalled its ambassador from Israel, citing “the unprecedented tide of deadly violence” inside Gaza.  

Chadian alignment with the UAE is not only military. As previously reported by MEE, the Emiratis offered Deby “more than a billion dollars” to “flip Chad towards supporting the RSF” after the war in Sudan began, according to former CIA analyst Cameron Hudson.

Senior UAE and regional officials referred to ICC over role in Sudan atrocities

Read More »

That figure now looks like loose change. In May 2025, in Abu Dhabi, Chad unveiled Chad Connexion 2030, a $30bn national development strategy to remake the infrastructure of a landlocked country from the ground up.

The UAE was, by a wide margin, its most important bilateral underwriter, securing $20.5bn in total backing and signing 18 contracts of its own worth over $6.2bn. 

Among the headline projects: an 800-km Etihad rail line to Cameroon’s port of Douala, a 50 MWp solar plant by Global South Utilities, industrial zones, Abu Dhabi Ports logistics hubs, and critical-mineral exploration permits. 

The partnership has tightened Chad’s dependence on the UAE and has become, in effect, the economic lifeline of Deby’s administration. To the west, Chad is already at odds with its neighbour Niger, which has drawn closer to Algeria.

In late October, Algeria deployed troops to Niger, the first time it had done this outside its borders since 1973. The move came days after Niger’s military government survived a coup attempt on 28 August.

Algeria’s move into Niger, according to the retired Algerian diplomat Amar Belani, is designed to counter what he described as “a destabilisation strategy actively involving the United Arab Emirates, Morocco, Israel and certain French proxies.”

The current geopolitical shifts, Belani went on, together with all they entail by way of rivalry and intervention by foreign actors, mean that “new tools, such as a show of presence including at the military level, are no longer a taboo and will be utilised to draw and reinforce Algeria’s red lines.”

Borderlands unrest

What is forming, in other words, is not one war but two rival blocs assembling around unrest in the desert borderlands. 

Rape, ransom and execution: The road out of Sudan's el-Fasher

Read More »

On one side: the Sudanese Armed Forces (which receives backing from Egypt and Turkey), Niger, Algeria, and the Tubu in Libya and Chad. On the other: the RSF, the Haftars, the UAE, Ethiopia and the Chadian state, with the French leaning towards this camp.

And the local fights and the larger one are no longer separate. A mining dispute in a town of a few thousand people tucked away deep in the remote mountains of Chad has become entangled with an arms corridor sustaining one of the world’s deadliest wars, with a succession contest inside Libya’s eastern military establishment, and a Sahelian realignment redrawing alliances from Algiers to Khartoum. 

“We do not want to be part of a bigger game,” one member of the Tubu defence committee in Miski told MEE. “We just want peace and justice and foremost, transparency in mining and the development of our region.”

But whether it remains a local counter-insurgency or becomes the spark for something larger will depend less on what happens in the mountains of Tibesti than on decisions being made in Abu Dhabi, Benghazi and Paris.

Sahel

Oscar Rickett

Miski, Chad

articles.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes
articles.summary:
Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery in retaliation for deadly strikes

Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 15:56

Yemeni movement says the refinery attack was in retaliation to Saudi strikes, including one that killed at least 26 people earlier this week

This satellite image shows a large smoke cloud billowing over Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery on 25 November 2026 (Planet Labs PBC/Handout via Reuters)

Off

Yemen's Houthi movement claimed responsibility for an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery, Ras Tanura, on Wednesday, describing it as retaliation for repeated Saudi strikes that have killed scores of civilians.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that the refinery attack caused fires and came in retaliation for the "brutal Saudi aggression against our country, including its targeting of passenger buses and citizens' trucks in the Al-Maqatirah district of Lahij, as well as other crimes in the capital, Sanaa, and the governorates."

The attack in the district of Lahij earlier this week killed at least 26 people.

In a follow-up post on X, Saree responded to Saudi threats to retaliate against Yemen's civilian Hodeidah port, which Saudi Arabia has already bombed, by warning that all "enemy Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast will be targets".

"We warn employees, workers and those near these ports to evacuate them immediately and stay away, and we call on all shipping companies to remove their ships from those ports immediately," the post added.

Ansar Allah, known as the Houthis, which controls the capital Sanaa and much of north and western Yemen, has been firing missiles at Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and office buildings since Yemen's frozen civil war reignited in July in a spillover from the Israeli-US war on Iran.

Riyadh broke the ceasefire, which also included Saudi Arabia, when it bombed Sanaa's international airport on 13 July.

Since then, the Saudi military has struggled to contain the Houthis and their ability to counter Saudi-backed forces in Yemen.

The ongoing attacks are wreaking havoc on the Saudi economy, oil infrastructure and the country's international image.

Airlines have cancelled international flights from the Saudi capital, Riyadh, while previous attacks on the country’s oil infrastructure have disrupted oil supplies.

The attacks have also forced Saudi Arabia to postpone or cancel major international events, including football's AFC Asian Cup and the flagship Future Investment Initiative conference.

Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudis said that air defences had intercepted and destroyed four drones in Ras Tanura in the country's Eastern Province. They did not deny that the attack had struck the oil refinery there.

Who are Yemen's Houthis and what do they want?

Read More »

Satellite images reviewed by Reuters showed large swathes of thick black smoke around the refinery, covering an area spanning around 600 square kilometres.

The Houthis have previously targeted Ras Tanura, which has a refining capacity of 550,000 barrels per day, during the conflict.

The refinery forms part of a strategic complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast facing Iran, through which the country exported most of its oil before the Israel-US war on Iran started on 28 February.

Since then, Saudi Arabia has had to send some of its oil through Yanbu on the west coast along the Red Sea, which receives oil via the East-West pipeline and has also faced attacks.

Separately, Houthi spokesman Saree had also said the group had attacked Riyadh's financial district in three phases.

Saudi civil defence said a strike on Tuesday wounded 11 people at a tower in Riyadh’s financial district. The tallest building in the capital, the tower houses the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, the kingdom’s sovereign wealth fund. It was the second strike on the tower in less than a week.

The first, on 19 November, damaged the building but caused no injuries. Saudi civil defence posted an image on Tuesday of the landmark tower showing some damage about halfway up the facade, similar to the impact of last week's attack.

articles.title: Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib join politicians and legal groups condemning Ulm 5 prosecution
articles.summary:
Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib join politicians and legal groups condemning Ulm 5 prosecution

Submitted by
Katherine Hearst
on
Wed, 11/25/2026 - 13:02

Two letters signed by 26 politicians and 31 legal groups demand the 'immediate release' of defendants in Germany

The 'Ulm Five' from left to right: Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo (supplied)

Off

Jeremy Corbyn and Rashida Tlaib are among dozens of politicians and legal organisations raising alarm over the prosecution and treatment of pro-Palestine activists in Germany.

Two letters issued on Wednesday, signed by 26 politicians and 31 legal groups from across the globe, condemned the treatment of five activists who have been held in pretrial detention for over 14 months.

Daniel Tatlow-Devally, Zo Hailu, Crow Tricks, Vi Kovarbasic and Leandra Rollo, who are from Germany, Spain, Ireland and the UK, were arrested on 8 September following an alleged break-in at the premises of Israeli arms firm Elbit Systems in the southwestern German city of Ulm.

Known as the “Ulm Five”, the group is accused of damaging the building's glass facade and smashing office equipment, including computers, screens and telephones.

In addition to charges of trespass and damage to property, the five are accused of "membership of a criminal organisation", namely Palestine Action Germany, under Section 129 of the German penal code.

The legislation is typically used to target organised crime networks and carries a potential sentence of up to five years in prison.

All the defendants have been held in prolonged pretrial detention, where they report facing restrictive conditions.

Under Section 129, suspects can be held for up to six months before trial, though lawyers say this period has now been significantly extended.

In their letter, the elected officials - including members of the German Bundestag, the European Parliament, the US Congress, the Irish Parliament and other legislatures across Europe and the Americas - called for the activists’ “immediate release”.

They further warned that the implications of their prosecution and treatment extend beyond the five defendants, forming “part of an international effort to discipline opposition to war and to place the interests of arms manufacturers above the rights of peoples and the obligations of international law”.

'Politically inconvenient facts'

Meanwhile, a separate letter signed by 33 legal groups - including the Center for Constitutional Rights, the Punjab Bar Council, European Democratic Lawyers, the American Association of Jurists, the Irish Council for Civil Liberties, the German Association of Democratic Lawyers - warned that the conduct of the trial could constitute a breach of German and international law.

In particular, the letter raises concerns about the courtroom’s security arrangements, which it said obstruct confidential communication between the defendants and their lawyers and could undermine the presumption of justice.

MEE previously reported that the trial, which began on 27 April, is taking place at a high security courtroom in the notorious Stammheim complex.

The defence team has repeatedly protested their clients’ treatment during proceedings, where the defendants are handcuffed and seated behind a glass barrier, preventing confidential communication with their lawyers.

The legal groups also challenged the court’s rejection of multiple applications by defence lawyers to hear expert witnesses. 

MEE previously reported that the court refused to hear weapons expert Dr Shir Hever and international law expert Isabel Feichtner, who were presented by the defence team to give evidence regarding Elbit Systems’ role in Israel’s genocide in Gaza and Germany’s obligations under international law.

The organisations further rejected the use of Section 129 against the defendants, insisting that “the prosecution of specific acts of property damage must not be conflated with the criminalisation of a political protest movement”.

"A criminal trial must establish the relevant facts impartially," they urged. "It must not exclude politically inconvenient facts merely because they concern the conduct of a powerful arms manufacturer or the actions of a state in an ongoing armed conflict".

articles.title: Unidentified drone enters Latvian airspace: military launches interceptor UAV
articles.summary:
An unidentified drone briefly entered Latvian airspace on the night of 26-27 November, prompting air-raid warnings in Ludza and Balvi municipalities.

Source: European Pravda, citing a statement by the Latvian National Armed Forces

Details: The military detected a drone close to Latvia's border on Friday night. It briefly entered Latvian airspace. At 02:30, an orange alert – indicating a detected threat in Latvian airspace and requiring residents to seek safety indoors and follow official instructions – was issued in Ludza Municipality.

Fighter jets from NATO's Baltic Air Policing mission were scrambled in response. Latvian forces also launched an interceptor drone to shoot down the threat. The interceptor returned to its launch site after the flight. Air defence units were on standby to respond immediately.

The threat to the airspace in Ludza Municipality ended at 02:55, and the all-clear was given.

A yellow alert regarding a possible airspace threat was also issued in Balvi Municipality. It was lifted at around 03:30 after the threat had passed.

Ukrainian drones also attacked Russia's Leningrad Oblast last night.

Latvia's National Armed Forces warned that similar incursions by unidentified drones could recur as long as Russia's aggression against Ukraine continues.

The military urged residents to remain vigilant, follow official updates and abide by the instructions sent through the mobile alert system.

Background:

On 11 November, three unmanned aerial vehicles entered Latvian airspace, two of which briefly (for one to two minutes) crossed the country's eastern border, while one crossed Latvia from south to north.

On the night of 2-3 November, an airspace threat was declared in Latvia's Ludza and Balvi municipalities due to an unidentified drone; the object crashed in the Balvi area.

On 1 November, the Latvian Armed Forces deployed an interceptor drone after an unidentified drone entered Latvian airspace. The unidentified drone later left Latvian airspace, and the military activated the interceptor's self-destruct mechanism.
